the place where Mormons hoped to establish a New Jerusalem or City of Zion; expelled in 1833
a small town the church bought and renamed, where it lived with a degree of peace and prosperity for a few years

marks: Joseph Smith said that God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to him in a vision in the spring of 1820.

notes: Joseph Smith says that in the spring of 1820 God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to him and told him to join none of the existing churches.
Smith publishes the Book of Mormon, said to be translated from golden plates, and organises the Church of Christ.
Mormons are expelled from Jackson County, Missouri, after moving west from New York and Ohio.
After fighting between Missourians and Mormons the governor of Missouri issues an extermination order, and the Mormons flee the state.
Smith is killed by a mob, precipitating a succession crisis; the largest group follows Brigham Young to what became the Utah Territory.
Church president Wilford Woodruff announces the official end of plural marriage; several small groups later break away as Mormon fundamentalist denominations.
The LDS Church abandons the exclusion of black men from the priesthood.
The LDS Church begins a push to distance itself from the label Mormonism; membership is claimed at 16 million in 2020.
